title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). X = D_0 is a complex analytic space, here a compactified moduli space \bar M_{g,ν}, with a normal crossings divisor D (the boundary). D_d is the normalization of the codimension-d stratum: its points are pairs (x, an unordered set of d local branches of D through x). Θ_d is the induced normal crossings divisor on D_d, and D_d^* = D_d \ Θ_d is the open stratum. Earlier he introduced D_{d,d'} for d ≥ d'. A point of D_{d,d'} is a point of D_d with a chosen subset of d' of its d branches. There are 'generalization' homomorphisms π_1 P_d^* → π_1 P_{d'}^*, where P_d is a torsor over D_d under an (extended) analytic group G_d. P_d is essentially the torus of normal directions, so P_d^* plays the role of a deleted tubular neighbourhood, or link, of the stratum.

This page.

(1) Flag spaces. For d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_r ≥ 0 he defines D_{d_0,…,d_r}. A point is a point of D_{d_0} together with a flag of subsets of its set of d_0 branches, of cardinalities d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_r. Their disjoint union is D_{Δ_r}, where Δ_r = [0,r]∩N is the standard ordered r-simplex. This agrees with an earlier notation D_J for a finite ordered set J.

(2) Simplicial structure. An increasing map φ: Δ_s → Δ_r induces D_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_s}, sending (x, flag) to (the point of D_{d_φ(0)} given by the d_φ(0) branches, subflag). So 𝒟_* is a simplicial analytic space; '1/2-simplicial' is the old 'semi-simplicial', i.e. simplicial. Equivalently, D_{d_0,d_1,d_2} = D_{d_0,d_1} ×_{D_{d_1}} D_{d_1,d_2}, and so on. Thus 𝒟_* is the nerve of an internal category in analytic spaces: objects ∐_d D_d, morphisms ∐_{d≥d'} D_{d,d'}. This is the 'category of strata' of the normal crossings divisor.

(3) Formula (205). The face map D_{d_*} → D_{d_0} ('first component') is finite étale. Concretely, D_{d_*} = D^!_{d_0} ∧^{𝔖_{d_0}}_{D_{d_0}} F_{d_*}(I_{d_0}). Here D^!_{d_0} is the 𝔖_{d_0}-torsor of numberings of the branches, and F_{d_*}(I_{d_0}) is the finite 𝔖_{d_0}-set of flags of type d_* in I_{d_0} = {1,…,d_0}.

(4) Open parts. D^*_{d_0,…,d_r} is the inverse image of D^*_{d_0}, i.e. the complement of the pulled-back divisor Θ_{d_0}.

The next page pulls back the torsors P_{d_0} and groups G_{d_0} along the first-vertex map. It then writes 2-cartesian squares of fundamental groupoids, Π_1 P^*_{d_*} → Π_1 P^*_{d_0} over Π_1 D_{d_*} → Π_1 D_{d_0}.

Purpose: to assemble the fundamental groupoids of the boundary links into a simplicial diagram of groupoids indexed by the nerve of the stratum category. Its 2-colimit / descent data should describe the 'structure à l'infini', i.e. the fundamental groupoid of a deleted tubular neighbourhood of the boundary of M_{g,ν}. This is a van Kampen/descent-type gluing along the stratification.
errors: (204): the index set should be N^{r+1}, not N^r. The ordering condition under the coproduct is written '>' but should be '≥' (as in line 2 of the page).

(205) is an abuse as transcribed. The contracted product needs the 𝔖_{d_0}-torsor of numberings over D_{d_0}, not D_{d_0} itself. The image suggests Grothendieck wrote D^!_{d_0} for that torsor, which makes the formula correct.
The final sentence refers to an 'image inverse Δ_{d_0-d_r}'; the index is unclear and is probably just a name for the pulled-back divisor. It is harmless.

ideas.what: Simplicial space of flags of branches of a normal crossings divisor, i.e. the nerve of the internal category of normalized strata with 'forget branches' maps
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of the stratification (category of strata / exit-path-type category); semi-simplicial resolution of a normal crossings divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Hodge II/III (semi-simplicial resolutions by normalized strata), 1971–74; exit-path categories: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie

ideas.what: Flag strata as finite étale covers: contracted product of the numbering torsor with the 𝔖_{d_0}-set of flags
ideas.modern_name: Associated finite étale cover of a torsor (contracted product)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 (torsors, Galois theory of finite étale covers), as a general technique

ideas.what: Pulling back the link torsors P_d / groups G_d along the simplicial space to obtain a simplicial diagram of fundamental groupoids (2-cartesian squares) describing the homotopy type at infinity of M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Gluing of boundary link groupoids; cf. Kato–Nakayama spaces / real oriented blow-up and Ihara–Nakamura boundary/tangential basepoint techniques
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions 'structure à l'infini' and tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary only informally

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν} as a simplicial analytic space (nerve of the stratum category) and plans to glue the fundamental groupoids of the boundary links along it via 2-cartesian squares. This is a combinatorial-simplicial framework for the profinite 'fundamental groupoid at infinity', anticipating later Kato–Nakayama/exit-path approaches. The individual ingredients are standard; only the systematic packaging for M_{g,ν} in the mid-1980s is of historical interest.
missed.quote: Alors D_{Δ_r} dépend fonctoriellement de façon contravariante de Δ_r, pour les applications croissantes, entre simplexes, donc on a un espace analytique 1/2-simplicial
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest for anabelian studies of the boundary of M_{g,n} (Ihara–Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki, Collas–Maugeais), which use similar boundary groupoids without this simplicial formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is setup and notation: a standard simplicial resolution by flag strata of a normal crossings divisor, plus a routine torsor description. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'structure à l'infini' programme but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: In (205) the '!' is most likely a superscript on D_{d_0} (D^!_{d_0}, the torsor of numberings), not over the '=' sign. The subscript D_{d_0} under the ∧^{(𝔖_{d_0})} indicates a contracted product over D_{d_0}.
In (204): the coproduct index set should read N^{r+1}, with d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_r.
The annotation under (205) reads roughly: 'ens. des "drapeaux de type d_*" de l'ens. fini I_{d_0}=[1,d_0]∩N' (correcting a struck word).
Line 7: 'ens. fini ordonné envisagé un peu plus haut (alinéa)' – the last word is likely 'alinéa'.
